It looks like overhead. Why not extend ITransactionService and use it in PaymentCleanupHostedService?
The split was intentional: ITransactionService handles transaction lifecycle while IPaymentGateway handles the external provider connection — different responsibilities.
Why does the engine level need to know about the gateway? Can't ITransactionService expose whether a payment can be processed?

The gateway abstraction may eventually expose retry policies, circuit-breaker state, and provider metadata — collapsing it into ITransactionService would widen that interface beyond its responsibility.
Why not just use IStockRepository here instead of introducing IInventoryStorageAccess?
IStockRepository manages individual stock records; IInventoryStorageAccess is about warehouse-level storage state (capacity, availability) — different levels of abstraction.
I don't see a reason why storage availability can't live in IStockRepository. How is this different from the CanFulfill method?

CanFulfill checks whether a specific SKU quantity can be fulfilled. IInventoryStorageAccess.IsAvailable checks whether the warehouse itself is reachable and healthy — broader scope. I'm open to renaming it to IWarehouseHealthAccess if that makes the distinction clearer.
fix!: Rename IInventoryStorageAccess to IWarehouseHealthAccess and update all usages. Verify the build and unit tests pass after the rename.
